newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares trade tight to close firm ahead of poll.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares trade tight to close firm ahead of poll.

text.p: Greek equities traded in a narrow range to close with mild gains while trading volume jumped to 16 billion drachmas. Brokers said trading was cautious mixed with speculative plays ahead of the national vote on Sunday.

"Overall the market traded cautiously in a tight range and really went nowhere as everyone is tuned to the election outcome on Sunday. There was speculative play on certain shares like Intracom," said a floor tarder.

He said the market would stage a strong rally if the socialists win Sunday's national polls and could take the index up to 1050 points next week. A more limited upside reaction was likely in the event of a win by the conservatives.

"There will be less of a runup if New Democracy prevails, we're likely to see a hiatus until the dust settles and the market gets used to new faces and policies. But it could turn out a much better performance further out. It remains to be seen," the trader said.

With conflicting polls on the election outcome the prudent trading tactic was to take some of the profits after the recent rally. But whatever party wins, the market's prospects are positive another broker told Reuters.
ING Barings changed its previous underweight rating of Greece's equity market to a buy after the decision to call early elections, analyst Yannis Protopapadakis told Reuters.
Greece will hold early elections September 22. Socialist Prime Minister Costas Simitis is running neck and neck with conservative challenger Miltiadis Evert.
He is pinning his hopes for victory on a mass, flag-waving rally in Athens on Friday evening, the last day of campaigning.
Polls show smaller parties claiming a bigger share of the pie in this snap election while the number of undecided voters remains unusually high only two days before the national poll, analysts said.
The Athens general share index closed 0.25 percent, or 2.45 points higher at 963.94 from Thursday's 961.49 close after opening at 961.69 points.
Turnover jumped to 16.9 billion drachmas from 7.4 billion on Thursday on volume of 5.6 million shares, helped by block trades in National Mortgage Bank, National Housing Bank and Mills St. George.

Gainers led losers 137 to 76 with 33 issues unchanged on 246 traded. Banks gained 0.41 percent, industrials eased 0.03 percent but construction jumped 2.02 percent. Small-caps moved 0.49 percent higher.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 552-570 at the close. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended down 20 drachmas at 4,050 after moderate trade.

The recently launched Merrill Lynch stock index call warrant based on a basket of 23 shares was quoted higher at 211.30-222.40 drachmas. It expires on January 9 1998 with a strike price of 1000. It was in the money at 1052.5.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 4,480-4,756 drachmas at the close.
